    Design system

    Every component in components/ui, documented with what it is for, when not to use it, a live example of its states, and the accessibility decisions behind it. Rendered here for the th locale; switch the URL prefix to see the other one.

    • Colour palette
    • Layout: Container, Stack, Cluster, Grid
    • Content: Heading, Prose, SummaryList, DataTable, Tag, StatusTag, banners, no tinted boxes...
    • Forms: TextInput, Select, Radios, DateInput, ErrorSummary...
    • Interactive: Button, Link, Tabs, Accordion, Dialog
    • Open data: Figure, BarChart, ColumnChart, KeyFigures, DocumentList, SectionNav, TableOfContents, RelatedLinks, CiteThis

    Colour palette and the fill-only rule

    Every ratio below is re-derived by npm run check:contrast from styles/tokens.css. Swatches read their background from the live CSS custom property, so what you see here is the value actually in effect in the current theme, not a copy that can drift out of sync.

    Container

    For: Centres page content and applies the page gutter. One per page, wrapping everything below the header.

    Not for: Inside another Container. Nesting doubles the gutter for no reason.

    Container content, capped at --width-content and gutter-padded

    Stack

    For: Vertical rhythm: a flex column with one consistent gap from the space scale.

    Not for: For a horizontal row, use Cluster. For a responsive card grid, use Grid.

    First
    Second
    Third

    Cluster

    For: A wrapping horizontal group: tag lists, filter chips, a row of buttons that should wrap at narrow widths rather than overflow (1.4.10).

    Not for: For a fixed-column grid, use Grid instead.

    Tag one
    Tag two
    A longer tag that helps show wrapping behaviour
    Tag four

    Grid

    For: An auto-fitting card grid. Columns are computed from a minimum column width, so it reflows on its own without breakpoints and never needs to scroll horizontally.

    Not for: For a data grid with real rows and columns, use DataTable.

    Card
    Card
    Card
    Card

    Heading

    For: Every heading on the site, at whatever depth the page outline needs.

    Not for: For text that only needs to look bold, not to be a heading. Use font weight utilities on a <p> instead.

    This is rendered with level 4

    The visual size always follows the tag, from typography.css. Pass visualLevel only when the outline depth and the type size genuinely need to diverge.

    Accessibility notes

    • Takes a required level prop rather than defaulting to h2, so a component cannot silently skip a level in the outline (1.3.1, 2.4.6).

    Prose

    For: Wraps rich text (Portable Text output, long-form guidance) and applies the reading measure so lines do not run the full width of a wide page.

    Not for: For a single short paragraph or a form hint, which do not need a constrained measure.

    This paragraph is capped at the reading measure for Thai, which is wider for Thai because Thai runs more characters per line at the same point size.

    A second paragraph shows the automatic spacing Prose applies between flow elements.

    SummaryList

    For: Key and value rows for a record: a form's own summary before submit, a policy's detail page, a shuttle stop's facts.

    Not for: For tabular data with more than one value per row, where DataTable fits better.

    Form
    Dormitory maintenance report
    Deadline
    Rolling, no fixed date
    Responsible body
    TUSC Tha Prachan
    Change

    Accessibility notes

    • Stacks key over value below sm rather than forcing a horizontal scroll (1.4.10).

    DataTable

    For: Genuinely tabular data: a timetable, a list with several comparable columns per row.

    Not for: For a simple key/value record, where SummaryList is the right, simpler pattern.

    Tag

    For: A category label: which of transport, welfare, activity or governance a piece of content belongs to.

    Not for: For a status (in progress, delivered, blocked). Use StatusTag, which always carries an icon and word as well as colour.

    TransportWelfareActivityGovernanceNeutral

    StatusTag

    For: A status: not started, in progress, delivered, blocked, dropped, or a form/search result state.

    Not for: Never with an empty label. A StatusTag with no visible word is a 1.4.1 bug, which is why label is required, not optional.

    DeliveredIn progressBlockedDroppedNot started

    InsetText

    For: A quoted or supplementary passage set off from the surrounding copy: a quote from a policy document, a worked example.

    Not for: For a warning, where WarningText carries the icon that a plain inset does not. Inset text has a grey rule and indented text, with no fill and no colour.

    A quoted passage sits here, indented and set off from the paragraph before it.

    WarningText

    For: A warning the reader needs to notice before continuing: a deadline that has nearly passed, a form that cannot be resubmitted.

    Not for: For a page-level alert about something that just happened, where NotificationBanner is the right pattern.

    !

    คำเตือน: ปิดรับคำร้องนี้ในอีก 2 วัน

    Accessibility notes

    • The GOV.UK warning text: bold text beside a black "!" icon, with no box, fill or coloured border. children must start with the visually hidden word "Warning" in the active language (UI.warning); the icon is decorative.

    Details

    For: Extra detail that most readers do not need: a definition, a longer explanation, an FAQ answer.

    Not for: For anything that must be visible on first load, or for a tooltip. Use it in place of a tooltip, not alongside one (1.4.13).

    What counts as a welfare emergency?

    Anything that puts a student's health, safety or ability to continue studying at immediate risk.

    NotificationBanner

    For: A page-level message: a form was submitted, a service is degraded, a warning that needs immediate attention.

    Not for: For a per-field form error, where ErrorMessage plus ErrorSummary is the correct pattern.

    Service notice

    The shuttle timetable was updated for this semester.

    Submitted

    Your report has been sent to TUSC Tha Prachan.

    Action needed

    This form closes for submissions in 2 days.

    Accessibility notes

    • The GOV.UK notification banner: a white body inside a solid border, with a solid title bar holding the title. Brand colour for info and warning, green for success. There is no tinted fill.
    • info is a labelled region; success is role=alert and takes focus when it appears after an action; warning is announced assertively (4.1.3).

    No tinted accent boxes

    For: Setting something apart from the text around it. This site uses the GOV.UK patterns: inset text for a quotation or supporting passage, warning text for something the reader must not miss, a notification banner for a page-level message, an error summary for a failed form, a phase banner for the service stage, and a summary card, a heading with a rule or a plain list for grouped information.

    Not for: A coloured or tinted background panel with a coloured left or top stripe, a coloured border, or both: a callout box, alert box or soft-tinted card. Do not use them on the public site or in the admin console. Use headings, spacing, rules and bold text for structure, and never let colour carry the meaning on its own.

    Summary card

    Student ID reissue form

    Used for a lost or damaged card. White, a thin grey border, and a title row above a rule.

    Accessibility notes

    • A small tinted fill behind a word is allowed on tags and status tags, which are labels, and the word and icon always come with it.
    • scripts/check-no-accent-boxes.mjs runs in npm run check and fails on a class list that pairs a coloured thick border with a tinted background, and on bg-*-soft outside the tag components.
    • Rich text callout blocks keep their stored tones: info renders as inset text, warning and critical as warning text. Service alerts render as notification banners, critical with warning text inside.

    Panel

    For: A prominent confirmation panel at the end of a completed task, such as a submitted form.

    Not for: Anywhere higher up a page than the very end of a completed flow, because it is deliberately prominent.

    Report submitted

    Your reference number is WF-2031.

    Pagination

    For: Paging through a long list: news, events, forms.

    Not for: For fewer results than fit on one page. It renders nothing when totalPages is 1 or fewer.

    EmptyState

    For: A list or search with nothing in it, so the page never looks broken or blank. Shows the River illustration above the title; pass illustration={false} to leave it out.

    Not for: For an error condition, where NotificationBanner variant="warning" fits better. Turn the illustration off in dense staff tables.

    No events scheduled

    Check back closer to the new semester.

    No events scheduled

    Accessibility notes

    • The illustration is decorative (aria-hidden), so the title is the only content a screen reader announces.

    River

    For: The small campus scene (sun, river and ferry) used in EmptyState, the not-found pages and the error page. Under 2 KB, coloured with fill and surface tokens so it follows the theme.

    Not for: As the only signal of a state, or anywhere it would repeat on the same page. It is decoration and has no meaning of its own.

    Accessibility notes

    • Renders aria-hidden and not focusable. Size it with className, for example h-[84px] w-[120px].

    Timestamp

    For: Any published, reviewed or updated date on the site.

    Not for: Never render a bare formatted date string without this component: the machine-readable datetime attribute is what lets assistive tech and search engines parse it unambiguously.

    date: 7 สิงหาคม 2569

    datetime: 7 สิงหาคม 2569 09:00

    relative: 3 เดือนที่ผ่านมา

    TextInput

    For: A single line of free text: a name, an email address, a reference number.

    Not for: For anything longer than a line, use Textarea. For a fixed set of choices, use Select or Radios.

    8 digits, no dashes

    Enter an email address in the correct format

    Accessibility notes

    • Label, hint and error are tied to the input via aria-describedby, built with describedBy() (3.3.1, 3.3.2).

    Textarea

    For: Free text of more than one line: a description, a message body.

    Not for: When there is a maximum length the reader should see counting down, where CharacterCount is the composed version of this same component.

    Describe what happened and where

    CharacterCount

    For: A Textarea with a maximum length the reader should see counting down: an emergency report body, for instance.

    Not for: For a field with no real length limit, where the count would just be noise.

    เหลือ 200 ตัวอักษร

    เหลือ 200 ตัวอักษร

    Accessibility notes

    • The visible count updates every keystroke; the version announced to assistive tech is debounced by 500ms so a fast typist is not interrupted mid-sentence (4.1.3).

    Select

    For: A single choice from a longer list, where showing every option as a radio would take too much space.

    Not for: For two to five options, where Radios keeps every choice visible at once and is easier to scan.

    Radios

    For: A small set of mutually exclusive choices, all visible at once.

    Not for: When more than one option can be true at the same time, where Checkboxes is correct.

    Where are you reporting from

    Accessibility notes

    • Grouped with a real <fieldset>/<legend> (via Fieldset), the native way to name a group of inputs, not an aria-label on a wrapping div.

    Checkboxes

    For: Any number of choices from a set, including none or all of them.

    Not for: For mutually exclusive choices, where Radios is correct.

    Which facilities need attention

    DateInput

    For: A date the reader types: a date of birth, a date something happened.

    Not for: For a date picked from a calendar of upcoming dates (an event booking), where a native input type="date" or a purpose-built calendar picker fits better.

    Date it happened

    Accessibility notes

    • Three separate fields rather than a native date picker: a native picker renders differently per browser and OS and cannot show the Buddhist year Thai readers expect.

    Fieldset

    For: Groups related controls under one legend. Radios, Checkboxes and DateInput all use this internally; reach for it directly only when composing a custom group of controls.

    Not for: Around a single control, which already has its own label.

    Contact preference

    Choose at least one

    Custom group content goes here, same as inside Radios or Checkboxes.

    ErrorMessage

    For: The inline error under a single field. TextInput, Textarea and Select render this for you when you pass error; use it directly only when building a custom field.

    Not for: Alone, without also listing the same error in ErrorSummary at the top of the form (3.3.1).

    Enter a value for this field

    ErrorSummary

    For: Lists every failing field at the top of a form after a failed submit, each one linking to its field by id.

    Not for: On a page with no form, or when there are no errors: it renders nothing when items is empty.

    There is a problem

    • Enter an email address in the correct format
    • Enter the date it happened

    Accessibility notes

    • autoFocus is the plain HTML attribute, not a scripted focus() call, so it moves focus here even on a full page reload with JavaScript off.
    • That means the live example below also grabs focus when this reference page itself loads or is revisited. That is correct production behaviour for a real failed submit, reproduced honestly here rather than faked with a non-functional copy; it is the one component on this page where loading it disturbs the page's own focus order.

    Button

    For: A primary action, a secondary action, a quiet inline action, or a destructive one. Renders <a> instead of <button> when given href, with identical styling.

    Not for: For plain navigation inside body copy, where Link is correct and keeps the underline readers expect on an inline link.

    As a link

    Accessibility notes

    • Every size clears the 24x24 CSS px target minimum via an explicit min-h/min-w, not only the global selector, so it holds even when rendered as <a> (2.5.8).
    • loading announces loadingLabel politely without changing the visible label text.

    Link

    For: An inline link inside body copy. Detects an external URL automatically and appends a visually-hidden new-tab notice.

    Not for: For a call-to-action that should look like a button, use Button with an href instead.

    Read the internal forms page, or the university website (เปิดในแท็บใหม่).

    Tabs

    For: A small, fixed set of views over the same subject, all visible at once conceptually: this semester's timetable by day, for instance.

    Not for: For a sequence the reader should read start to finish, or for more than about five panels, where a list of links to separate pages reads better.

    Panel content for Monday.

    Panel content for Tuesday.

    Panel content for Wednesday.

    Accessibility notes

    • Roving tabindex: only the selected tab sits in the Tab order, arrow keys move between tabs (WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern).

    Accordion

    For: A list of independent, optional sections a reader may or may not need: an FAQ, a set of guide chapters.

    Not for: For content the reader is very likely to need, which should just be visible.

    Use the lockers form under Welfare.

    Report it through the transport report form.

    Dialog

    For: A focused task that must be completed or dismissed before returning to the page: a confirmation before a destructive action.

    Not for: For anything that should stay reachable while the reader keeps working, or for a simple disclosure, where Details fits better.

    Confirm

    Escape, the close button, or the reader's own back gesture all close this. Nothing here ever blocks Escape.

    Accessibility notes

    • Native <dialog> with showModal(): focus trap and Escape-to-close are the browser's own behaviour. Nothing here calls preventDefault on cancel, so Escape always works.

    DataTable: row headers, totals and notes

    For: A table of figures. The first column becomes row headers, totals sit in a tfoot, numbers are right-aligned in tabular figures, and the source and numbered notes follow the table.

    Not for: For a handful of facts about one thing, where SummaryList reads better. Do not recompute a total the source states: show the stated total and say so in a note.

    Table 1: Budget by organisation, fiscal year 2569 (baht)

    ASA TPC volunteer clubClub313,000

    Student Council (TUSC)Council9,182[หมายเหตุ 1]

    Accessibility notes

    • rowHeader on a column renders th scope=row in the body and the footer, so a screen reader announces the organisation before each amount.
    • Footer rows are a real tfoot. On a phone they stack like body rows; a column left empty in a footer row is hidden.
    • NoteRef is a link to the numbered note below the table. Its text reads 'note 1' in full.

    Figure and BarChart

    For: A chart with its number, a title that states the finding, a subtitle, a source line, numbered notes and a download. Bars keep the order given, start at zero and carry their values.

    Not for: For a number with nothing to compare it to, use KeyFigures. A chart never replaces its table: put the same figures in a DataTable beside or below it.

    หมายเหตุ
    1. Sorted by amount. The report lists the organisations in a different order.
    ดาวน์โหลดข้อมูลรูปที่ 1
    • Budget by organisation (CSV, 1 KB)

    Accessibility notes

    • The SVG is one role=img named by its title and described by a 100 to 200 character alternative that opens 'A bar chart showing that'.
    • One colour for the bars and the accent for the bar the title is about. The highlight is named in the title and the alternative, so colour is never the only signal.
    • Colours are theme tokens, so the chart follows the light and dark themes. Nothing animates.
    • Notes and downloads are native disclosures that work without JavaScript.

    BarChart: year on year

    For: The same categories in two periods. The current period is a solid bar and the earlier one an outline beneath it, each labelled with its value.

    Not for: For more than two periods, where a ColumnChart in time order reads better.

    Accessibility notes

    • The legend names both series in words. The outline versus fill difference does not depend on colour.

    ColumnChart

    For: A short series in time order, such as attendance at each meeting, with an optional dashed reference line such as the number of seats.

    Not for: For comparing categories, where a sorted BarChart is easier to read. For a long series, where a line chart would be needed.

    Accessibility notes

    • The reference line is labelled on the chart and described in the alternative text. The dash pattern distinguishes it from the axis without colour.

    KeyFigures

    For: Two or three headline numbers at the top of a page, each with a label and the period it covers.

    Not for: For more than three numbers, or for a number whose meaning needs a comparison. Use a Figure.

    • Each tile is a list item with a heading, the figure as text and its context. The figure is kept to 14 characters so it does not wrap or overflow at 320px.

    DocumentList

    For: A list of documents to open or download: title, type, date, file format and size, and a line of description.

    Not for: For a single file, use DownloadList. For ordinary page links, use RelatedLinks.

    Accessibility notes

    • The link carries a visually hidden suffix with the format and size, so the link text is complete out of context. The visible file details are hidden from screen readers to avoid reading them twice.
    • A missing date is written out, such as '[date not stated]', never left blank.

    DownloadList

    For: A bare list of downloadable files. Each link states what it is, its type and its size.

    Not for: For documents with a description and a date, use DocumentList. Do not list a format that does not exist yet.

    • Budget by organisation (CSV, 1 KB)

    SectionNav

    For: Links between the pages of one section. A compact two-column list on a phone and a vertical list with a rule beside it from the md breakpoint.

    Not for: For the whole site, which is the header's job. For sections within one page, use TableOfContents.

    Accessibility notes

    • A nav landmark named by a visible label. The current page has aria-current=page and is bold with a dark bar, so it does not rely on colour.
    • Links are at least 44px tall on a phone and never scroll sideways.

    TableOfContents

    For: A numbered list of the sections on a long page, linking to their headings.

    Not for: For a page that fits on one screen. Keep the list shorter than the viewport.

    RelatedLinks

    For: A short list of related pages or datasets, each with an optional one-line description.

    Not for: For the main route through a page, which belongs in the content.

    CiteThis

    For: A ready-made reference at the foot of a data page.

    Not for: For credit to a person or a photograph. Use the page's own source line.

    Accessibility notes

    • The current page is a link with aria-current=page and is drawn solid and bold. Gaps are hidden from assistive technology.
    • Every page is a real URL from buildHref, so it works without JavaScript. The numbers wrap at 320px instead of scrolling.
